solutions.check: 32 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Chuck, way before Brenda's devious counsel

indicators.note: placing one thing before another tells you the order the parts are joined in

blocks.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda, and ER is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A lawyer tricks some chap called Chuck on behalf of a woman named Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye nicknames the Queen 'Brenda', so 'Brenda's' leads to ER, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a slang term for an unscrupulous lawyer, one who gives crooked legal advice.

clue.text: Drink breaks as announced by one who's pissed?

indicators.text: as announced by one who's pissed
indicators.note: a drunk slurs words, so we hear the word as a drunkard would pronounce it

blocks.note: breaks means snaps, slurred with a drunken 'sh'

explanation.surface: A drink is knocked over or smashed by someone who is already drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' is British slang for drunk, and a drunk turns S into SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit, a kind of alcoholic drink originally from Germany.

clue.text: Y-fronts extremely constricting of organ, producing periods

indicators.note: at the extremes means the outermost letters only
constricting means squeezing round something, holding it inside

blocks.note: the outer letters of the underwear name
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Tight underpants squeezing a man's privates, with painful results.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ suggests something lower down, but it is the ear. Y-fronts are British men's briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Years are periods of time, so the plural noun matches the plural definition.

clue.text: The Eye is able to enter the boundaries of Tony's holiday place

indicators.note: entering the boundaries of a word means going between its outer letters

blocks.note: first boundary letter of the name
Private Eye speaks of itself as 'us'
is able means can
last boundary letter of the name

explanation.surface: The magazine gatecrashes Tony Blair's Italian holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tony's' does double duty in the surface, but the definition is just 'holiday place'; the name supplies its outer letters. Tony Blair famously holidayed in Tuscany.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany, the Italian region, is a favourite summer retreat for British visitors, Tony Blair among them.

clue.text: And, as Merkels said (after Balls in an outburst), "Not necessary"

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: a rant is an outburst; its first part
Ed Balls, the Labour politician
und is German for 'and', as Angela Merkel would say
the rest of the rant

explanation.surface: German chancellor Merkel rejects Ed Balls's tirade as pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls was a Labour shadow chancellor and Angela Merkel the German chancellor, so 'Merkels said' points to German.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundant means superfluous, no longer needed, which is what not necessary says.

clue.text: Professional with means of spying anal sex exponent?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone whose trade is planting listening devices
second meaning: the coarse literal sense of the word

explanation.surface: A spy who is also notorious for his sexual tastes, in the Private Eye manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal, one who plants bugs; the second is the vulgar original meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who plants hidden microphones and, in its old legal sense, one who commits sodomy.

clue.text: Increase what you have and get stuffed

blocks.note: to up something is to increase it
what you have is yours

explanation.surface: Advice to grow your holdings, followed by a rude dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are vulgar dismissive retorts telling someone to go away in contempt.

clue.text: Dread getting screwed in ugly squalor, having taken precautions

indicators.note: something screwed is twisted out of shape, so its letters are mixed
squalor is mess and disorder, so these letters are in a jumble too
being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: first part of the rearranged word
this word rearranged
rest of the rearranged word

explanation.surface: Someone who fears being swindled in grim surroundings proceeds cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having taken precautions' doubles as a sexual joke, in keeping with 'screwed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardedly means cautiously, in a careful way, as someone who has taken precautions acts.

clue.text: Party gathering truly doesn't have Clegg's heart in it

indicators.note: not having something means it is left out
the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: truly means really
the middle letter of the Lib Dem leader's name

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem conference lacks Nick Clegg's real commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats; removing his heart from the word for truly leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a mass meeting of supporters, the sort of gathering a political party holds.

clue.text: see 10ac.
(& 9/19) Kitchen waste stuffed inside loaf, bun – bastards responsible are going to suffer!

definitions.text: bastards responsible are going to suffer!

indicators.note: something stuffed inside is packed into the middle of what follows

blocks.note: loaf is slang for the head, as in 'use your loaf'
swill is kitchen scraps fed to pigs
a bun is a bread roll

explanation.surface: Someone finds rubbish baked into their bread and vows revenge on the bakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is rhyming slang, loaf of bread for head. Swill is the scraps fed to pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'heads will roll' predicts that those to blame will be sacked or punished.

clue.text: Cleaner gets outspoken bloke's rag

indicators.note: speaking out means saying the word, so we want something said rather than spelt

blocks.note: a daily is a cleaning woman who comes in each day
a bloke is a man, a male

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady picks up the tabloid some loudmouth man left lying about.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a domestic cleaner. Private Eye habitually calls the Daily Mail a rag.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a dismissive word for a low-grade newspaper, and the Daily Mail is a British tabloid.

clue.text: Muscles ain't working, so lay off the sex?

indicators.note: working here means being worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: abs are abdominal muscles
the letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: If your muscles have given up, perhaps it is time to give sex a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from something, here from sexual activity, the commonest use of the verb.

clue.text: The one French doctor getting to bottom of Sarkozy's dirty washing

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)
un is French for 'one'
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
the last letter of the former French president's name

explanation.surface: A French physician uncovers the truth about a French president's private life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs both 'The' and 'one'. Dirty washing aired in public is the usual Private Eye fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry is clothing and linen waiting to be cleaned, that is, the dirty washing pile.

clue.text: (& 22dn.) Cabinet ministers quite aloof from this sort of reception (odious with one initially divisive row)?

definitions.text: Cabinet ministers quite aloof from this sort
definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the people ministers keep their distance from

blocks.note: a reception is a party
rank means foul or offensive
with means together with, and
a file is a line or row, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: Ministers snub a reception full of unpleasant people where a row breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'one initially divisive' are surface colour; the row itself is the last piece. The rank and file are the ordinary members, below the leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: The party rank and file are ordinary grassroots members, whom senior ministers tend to hold at arm's length.

clue.text: President putting short jumpers on First Lady (large tits opening)

indicators.note: a short form drops the end of a longer word
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: kangaroos are jumpers, shortened to roos
Eve was the first woman
L is the abbreviation for large
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A president dresses his wife in revealing knitwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a president's wife, which suits the surface, but it is Eve. Jumpers are British sweaters too, another false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt was the surname of two US presidents, Theodore and Franklin D.

clue.text: ''Milking us rotten,'' the people cried when he passed

definitions.text: the people cried when he passed

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed out of shape, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Oppressed subjects complain of being exploited by a ruler, yet weep at his death.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim Il Sung, North Korea's founding dictator, died in 1994 to staged mass public mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: North Koreans were filmed wailing in the streets at the death of their leader in 1994.

clue.text: (& 28ac.) There's a bigger problem than this party copy of Private Eye?

definitions.text: There's a bigger problem than this

blocks.note: a party to a dispute is one side
each copy of a magazine belongs to an issue

explanation.surface: The magazine shrugs off a party's complaint about one of its editions as small beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a secondary matter, one less important than the main problem.

clue.text: Pervy groper's reached far side of anus passage

indicators.note: pervy means perverted, twisted, so the letters are bent out of order
the far side of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A lewd scene of a groper's hand making its way somewhere it shouldn't.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress means onward movement, the passage of something forward in time or space.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Chuck needs rest, badly, being one getting stuck into pot?

indicators.note: done badly, the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: to lob is to throw
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Chuck is exhausted and stoned on cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot suggests cannabis, but it is a lobster pot, the trap the creature crawls into, or the cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobsters are caught in lobster pots and boiled in cooking pots, so the crustacean is stuck in one.

clue.text: The cat regarded you coarsely as an 'adventurous character'

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
regarded means looked at, saw
yer is a rough, colloquial way of saying 'you'

explanation.surface: A cat stares rudely at someone and calls them an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks on 'adventurous character' hint at The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, the Mark Twain novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is the boy hero of Mark Twain's novel of adventures on the Mississippi.

clue.text: see 14ac.
"Try to escape the sack," said a lousy type

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the sound of the phrase matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: to try to escape is to flee
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: Someone facing dismissal is told to run before being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lousy' works literally, infested with lice, as a fleabag is.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleabag is a dirty, verminous person, so literally a lousy, louse-ridden type.

clue.text: Stage girl with nothing on meets Queen?

blocks.note: Flo is a girl's name
O is zero, nothing
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A naked actress is introduced to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage girl with nothing on' sounds like a showgirl, but stage is the definition, a storey or level of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor is one level of a building, and stage can mean such a storey or tier.

clue.text: Artist quit before "yes" from Fergie

blocks.note: to go is to leave, quit
ya is a posh, Sloaney 'yes', as the Duchess of York might say

explanation.surface: A painter resigns once Sarah Ferguson agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: Fergie is Sarah Ferguson, Duchess of York, mocked for a Sloane Ranger accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the Spanish painter of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Spotty thing (American) gives female infection

blocks.note: a lady is a woman
a bug is a minor infection

explanation.surface: A spotty American passes on an infection to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotty suggests acne, but the definition is the spotted beetle; ladybug is the American name for the British ladybird.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybug, the US word for ladybird, is a small beetle with black spots on red wing cases.

clue.text: Being right out of underwear set, sadly, ensure flesh stays succulent

indicators.note: being out of something means it is missing, so a letter is removed
things gone sadly have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
a bra is an item of underwear
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stripping off a lingerie set is told to keep their skin moist.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R out of BRA SET, then rearrange the letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste is to spoon fat or juices over meat while roasting so it stays moist.

clue.text: Public office first and foremost, dear solver, so speak now

indicators.note: the first and foremost part of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: overt means open, done in public
the opening letter of this word
the setter addressing the solver directly

explanation.surface: An invitation to the reader to pipe up about a public office.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay breaks the letters in a different place from the phrase's own word breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Over to you' hands the turn to another person, inviting them to talk next.

clue.text: see 17ac.
Kind of club that would make Balls a Tory (right wing, anyway)

indicators.note: to balls something up is to make a mess of it, so the letters get jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Ed Balls, a Labour politician, would need to be a club to become a Tory, given his politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls is a Labour politician, so 'Balls' looks like a name, but here it is the verb balls up. 'Wing, anyway' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary is a type of service club, Rotary International, whose local branches meet regularly.

clue.text: Pop group wants new lead on which shirt might be put?

definitions.text: on which shirt might be put

indicators.note: a new lead means the opening letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: the Bee Gees were a pop group of the Gibb brothers

explanation.surface: A band needs a new frontman, and his stage shirt is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: To put your shirt on something is to bet everything on it; gee-gees is British baby-talk for racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee-gees are racehorses, and putting your shirt on a horse means staking everything on it.
